records.name: Cartesian Inheritance Explosion
records.definition: Modeling every combination of two independent dimensions as its own subclass, so the class count grows multiplicatively.

records.name: Direct Access
records.definition: Reaching a resource directly with no intermediary, bypassing the access control, caching, or laziness a proxy would add.

records.name: Direct External Coupling
records.definition: Coupling code directly to an incompatible external interface, spreading its idiosyncrasies through the codebase.

records.name: Leaf-vs-Container Special-Casing
records.definition: Branching client code on whether an element is a leaf or a container instead of treating them through one interface.

records.name: Leaky Subsystem API
records.definition: Exposing a subsystem's internal complexity directly to clients instead of hiding it behind a simplifying interface.

records.name: Per-Instance Duplicate State
records.definition: Storing identical shared state separately in every object instance, wasting memory at high object counts.

records.name: Subclass Explosion
records.definition: Creating a distinct subclass for every combination of optional features instead of composing them at runtime.

records.name: High-Cardinality Object Reuse
records.definition: The ability to represent large numbers of similar objects economically by sharing their common intrinsic state.

records.name: Implementation Swap
records.definition: The ability to change an abstraction's underlying implementation without altering the abstraction itself.

records.name: Lazy Load
records.definition: The ability to defer creating or loading a costly resource until it is first used.

records.name: Leaf/Composite Transparency
records.definition: The ability to treat individual objects and compositions of objects through one uniform interface.

records.name: Recursive Composition

distinctFrom.reason: Recursive composition nests composites to any depth, while leaf and composite transparency lets callers treat both through one interface.

records.definition: The ability to build tree structures in which composites contain other composites to arbitrary depth.

records.name: Runtime Behavior Extension
records.definition: The ability to add responsibilities to an object dynamically at runtime by wrapping it.

records.name: Shared Immutable State

distinctFrom.reason: Shared immutable state is one object safely used in many contexts, while high-cardinality reuse represents many similar objects cheaply through that sharing.

records.definition: The ability to safely share one immutable state object across many contexts at once.

records.name: Simplified Access
records.definition: The ability to use a complex subsystem through a small, convenient interface.

records.name: Remote Stub
records.definition: A local stand-in object that forwards calls to an object living in another process or machine.

records.name: Common Interface
records.definition: The requirement that a wrapper and the object it wraps share one interface so they remain interchangeable.

records.name: Incompatible Interfaces
records.definition: A precondition of two interfaces that must cooperate yet expose mismatched signatures.

records.name: Independent Variation Axes
records.definition: The requirement that an abstraction and its implementation vary along separate axes so they can be decoupled.

records.name: Separable Intrinsic State
records.definition: The requirement that an object's shared, context-independent state be separable from its per-use state.

records.name: Uniform Component Interface
records.definition: The requirement that leaves and composites implement one shared interface so clients treat them alike.

records.name: Indirection
records.definition: The degree of extra indirection introduced by separating an abstraction from its implementation.

records.name: Over-Centralization
records.definition: The degree to which routing all access through one facade concentrates responsibility and can bottleneck change.

records.name: Stack Debugging
records.definition: The degree to which layers of wrapping deepen the call stack and complicate debugging.

records.name: Subsystem Complexity
records.definition: The degree of internal complexity in a subsystem that motivates hiding it behind a facade.

records.name: Transparency / Debugging
records.definition: The degree to which interposing a proxy hides the real object and complicates tracing calls to it.
